title: k8s-node-provisioning-ephemeral-debug-scratchpad
content:
Context / root cause hypothesis:
- Sporadic node registration failures during autoscaling windows on dedicated clusters. Problem observed across both AWS and on-prem pilot racks. Symptoms: nodes come up, kubelet starts, node never shows Ready in the control plane or disappears after short time with message 'node not found' / registration errors in kubelet logs.

Recent timeline:
- 2024-10-10: Cluster autoscale triggered after warm traffic spike; 3 nodes added, 2 failed to stabilize.
- 2024-10-11: Repro experiment on staging with identical machine image; 1/3 repro.
- 2024-10-12..2024-10-30: Iterative attempts with different cloud-init timeouts, kubelet flags, containerd version pinned/unpinned.

What I tried (commands + outputs / observations):

1) Basic node/registration checks
$ kubectl get nodes --watch
# Output: new-node-07 NotReady -> then disappears after ~90s

$ kubectl describe node new-node-07
# Output snippet: "Conditions: Ready False Unknown -- Kubelet not responding, LastHeartbeatTime: ..."

2) On-host: check kubelet service and journal
$ ssh ubuntu@new-node-07
$ sudo systemctl status kubelet -l
# kubelet active (running) but repeatedly restarts at boot in some cases (restart count ~3)
$ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
# key errors seen:
Oct 12 10:12:34 new-node-07 kubelet[1234]: E1012 10:12:34.123456    1234 kubelet.go:2205] Failed to register node with API server: nodes "new-node-07" not found
Oct 12 10:12:34 new-node-07 kubelet[1234]: W1012 10:12:34.123789    1234 server.go:xxxx] heartbeat failed: Post "https://api.redwood.internal:6443/api/v1/nodes/new-node-07/status": dial tcp 10.0.0.5:6443: connect: connection refused

Hypothesis A: kubelet starts before networking/CNI is fully configured, so initial registration attempts time out and API server rejections cause kubelet to backoff and loose state.
Hypothesis B: cloud-init timing leads to consistent ephemeral hostname drift (cloud-init sets hostname, but kubelet registered with different name), leading to 'node not found' vs duplicate node issues.
Hypothesis C: containerd CRI handshake/version mismatch causing kubelet failure to fully become Ready (seen logs referencing CRI handshake failure intermittently).

3) Inspect container runtime logs
$ sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager
# Observed: pull failures for some pause images, but most resolved on subsequent attempts.
2024-10-12T10:12:30Z containerd[900]: level=error msg="pulling image \"k8s.gcr.io/pause:3.6\": failed: Get \"https://...\": dial tcp: i/o timeout"

4) Helm / bootstrap chart checks
- Using helm chart infra/node-boot (internal) that runs a bootstrap DaemonSet to patch labels/taints once node joins. Chart run: helm upgrade --install node-boot ./charts/node-boot -n kube-system --wait --timeout 5m
- Observed: sometimes the DaemonSet never schedules on the failing node (since node not in Ready).

5) Reproduce with systemd-analyze to measure startup ordering
$ sudo systemd-analyze blame | head -20
# cloud-init-local.service 1min 2s
# cloud-init.service  45s
# docker/containerd   5s
# kubelet.service     3s
- cloud-init consistently delays; kubelet starts while cloud-init still running in some cases.

6) Quick experiment: postpone kubelet start via systemd override
$ sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d
$ echo -e "[Unit]
After=network-online.target cloud-init.service" | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-wait.conf
$ sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
- Result: node registration more stable in the single repro run.

Error snippets captured:
- "Failed to register node with API server: nodes \"new-node-07\" not found"
- "Post "https://api.redwood.internal:6443/api/v1/nodes/new-node-07/status": dial tcp 10.0.0.5:6443: connect: connection refused"
- "NodeController detected unreachable node, deleting" (observed on controller manager logs during transient network partition)
- containerd: "failed: i/o timeout" during image pull (intermittent)

Repro notes:
- Reproduces faster when provisioning in parallel (scale-up of 5+ nodes).
- More likely on older instance types with slower disk initialization (IO wait delays).

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Add systemd ordering change to defer kubelet until cloud-init and network-online are done (PR in infra image build: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678).
- Increase kubelet registration timeout (kubelet flag: --node-status-update-frequency or related) considered but not yet applied.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run extended stress repro: spin up 10 nodes in parallel, with and without systemd ordering change; log percentage of successful registrations.
- [ ] Add more robust retries around initial image pulls (containerd config: increase registry timeouts / mirrors).
- [ ] Audit cloud-init configuration to ensure consistent hostname set before kubelet starts. Check /etc/hostname vs kubelet --hostname-override.
- [ ] Investigate controller-manager logs for node eviction/deletion race (link to kube-controller-manager logs on masters).
- [ ] Add automated test in image pipeline that boots VM and verifies kubelet registers within 3m under simulated cold-disk conditions.
- [ ] If we still see errors after ordering fix, evaluate bumping kubelet backoff/retry config and adding preflight script that waits for containerd and network and pause-image availability.

Notes / sticky ideas:
- Could be multi-factor (cloud-init + slow disk + transient network). Ordering fix helps but doesn't fully eliminate failures at >5 parallel boots.
- Could add an init container on node-boot DaemonSet to detect node UUID mismatch and attempt to re-register (risky / hacky). Prefer fix at provisioning image level.
- Related tickets: PLAT-2345 (main incident), PLAT-2399 (follow-up image change).

Logs & links: (local copies in infra/logs/ and cluster controller logs)
- Master kube-apiserver/controller log excerpt (attached to JIRA PLAT-2345)
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR#678 (systemd ordering change)
- Repro script: scripts/scale-up-repro.sh 

Scratchpad commands to re-run when next investigating:
- scale-up repro (use local kubeconfig to staging): 
  ./scripts/scale-up-repro.sh --count 8 --image=ami-xxx --wait=600 | tee repro-$(date +%s).log
- ssh into problem node and collect quick dump:
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 --no-pager > /tmp/kubelet.log; sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 500 --no-pager > /tmp/containerd.log; sudo dmesg > /tmp/dmesg.log; sudo lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MOUNTPOINT,ROTA > /tmp/lsblk.txt
- check apiserver reachability from node:
  curl -k https://api.redwood.internal:6443/healthz -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:10.0.0.5

If I stop here: current best candidate for short-term reduction in incidents is the systemd ordering change + improving containerd image pull resilience. Longer term: add image pipeline boot test + look for race in hostname assignment.

-- Jordan
